newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba to privatize its telephone company.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba to privatize its telephone company.

text.p: The Canadian province of Manitoba on Thursday passed legislation to turn provincially owned Manitoba Telephone System into a publicly traded company.
The share offer was estimated at between C$750-C$800 million and could be the largest single offering in Canada this calendar year, analysts said.
A prospectus must now be approved by the Manitoba Securities Commission before shares can be sold.
The 90-year-old firm was one of only two provincially owned telephone companies in Canada. The other is SaskTel, owned by the neighboring province of Saskatchewan.
The legislation bars any individual from owning more than 10 percent of MTS shares but a 25 percent limit on strategic partners was removed from the bill, provincial spokesman Roger Matas said.
MTS is one of nine member companies of Stentor, a group of Canadian telecommunications firms. It employs 3,700 people.
MTS has the highest debt ratio of any Canadian telco, at 78 percent, while most have debt-to-equity ratios in the 40 to 50 percent range. Its debt ratio was 91 percent in 1988.
MTS posted a net income of C$14.4 million in 1994 on operating revenues of C$530.8 million.
